Overview of The Colony Municipal Court

The Colony Municipal Court is located in Denton County, Texas, with jurisdiction over various types of cases, including criminal offenses, traffic violations, and municipal ordinance violations. The court's mission is to provide efficient, courteous, and professional service to all members of the community.

How to Access Case Records

The Colony court records can be accessed through the town clerk’s and county clerk’s offices, as well as online. Records may be searched using the following methods:

  • By name
  • By case number
  • By address
  • By phone
  • By email

In some cases, record information may be confidential. To access such records, individuals must submit a record request form along with applicable fees.

Payment Options

Payments for fines and tickets at the Colony Municipal Court can be made in several ways:

1. In-Person

Visit the court during regular hours to pay with cash, checks, money orders, or credit cards (a 2.99% processing fee applies).

2. By Mail

Send a certified check or money order to: Colony Municipal Court
5151 N Colony Blvd,
The Colony, TX 75056,
United States
Do not send cash or personal checks by mail.

3. Online

Pay online through the Municipal Online Payments Portal. Enter your citation number and birth date to process your payment.

4. By Phone

Call 855-281-3560 to make a payment over the phone (service charges apply).

Resolving Citations

Citations issued by the Colony Municipal Court can be resolved in several ways before the due date:

  1. Submit a plea of guilty or no contest and pay the fine.
  2. Request a dismissal.
  3. Apply for a Driving Safety Course.
  4. Request a Deferred Disposition.
  5. Enter a plea of not guilty and request a trial.

For assistance, contact the court directly.

Traffic Violation Fines

Fines for traffic violations vary based on the specific offense. Examples include:

  • $200 for driving 1-9 miles over the speed limit.
  • $334 for driving 30+ miles over the speed limit.
  • $220 for driving with an invalid license.
  • $175 for operating with an expired registration.
  • $180 for not wearing a seatbelt.

Available Pleas

Individuals can submit one of three types of pleas for their citation:

  1. Plea of Guilty: Admit to the violation and receive a fine amount or court date.
  2. Plea of Not Guilty: Deny the violation; a trial date will be set for your defense.
  3. Plea of No Contest: Neither admit nor deny the charges; you may still qualify for a Driving Safety Course or Deferred Disposition.

Requesting a Deferred Disposition

To request a Deferred Disposition, visit the court or submit the form at the clerk’s office. You may be eligible if you meet certain criteria, including having a valid non-commercial driver’s license. There is a $20 administrative fee.

Appeals Process

If dissatisfied with a court decision, you can appeal by filing a motion for a new trial within 10 days of the ruling. If denied, you must file an appeal bond within the same timeframe.

FAQs

How can I appeal against the court’s decision?

You can appeal by submitting a motion for a new trial within 10 days of the decision. If your motion is denied, file an appeal bond within the same period.
